definition_zh: 电影；影片；电影院；看电影这项活动；电影业
definition_en: a film shown in a cinema or on a screen, also the cinema as a place or an outing and the film industry as a whole
core_image: 暗下来的放映厅里，一束光穿过空气打在幕布上
scene: 老街上的影院门口排起长队，售票窗口的灯还亮着。 They queued outside the old cinema for a late-night movie.
sceneCN: 这里是「电影、影片」（第 1 个义项：放映的故事片）；句意为他们为一场深夜电影在旧影院外排队。图中可辨识物件：影院门口、排队的人群、售票窗。

pos.zh: 电影；影片；电影院；看电影这项活动；电影业

derivatives.zh: 由 movie 与 goer 复合而成，义为「经常看电影的人」
由 movie 与 maker 复合而成，义为「电影制片人；导演」
由 movie 与 going 复合而成，义为「看电影这件事；常看电影的」

senses.title: A film shown on a screen
senses.definition: a story or record told in moving images and sound, shown in a cinema or on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 用活动影像和声音讲述的故事或记录，在影院或屏幕上放映
senses.example: We watched a movie about a fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看了一部关于渔村的电影。
senses.why: The word is a clipped form of moving picture, so the moving image itself is the starting point of every sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「活动的画面」的缩写，所以每一个义项都从「画面在动」这一点开始。

senses.title: The cinema as a place or an outing
senses.titleCN: 电影院；看电影这项活动
senses.definition: the cinema, or an occasion of going there to watch a film
senses.definitionCN: 电影院，或去那里看电影的一次活动
senses.example: They spent the afternoon at the movies.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一下午都泡在电影院里。
senses.why: Because a movie is what is shown, the plural the movies came to name the place and the outing built around it.
senses.whyCN: 因为被放映的东西是 movie，复数 the movies 就转而指放映它的场所，以及围绕它安排的一次出门。

senses.title: The film industry
senses.definition: the business of making and distributing films, especially in a particular country
senses.definitionCN: 制作与发行影片的行业，尤指某一国家的电影业
senses.example: He has worked in the movies for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在电影业干了三十年。
senses.why: A product made by many hands naturally names the whole trade that produces it, so the plural also stands for an industry.
senses.whyCN: 由许多人之手做出来的产品，自然会用来指生产它的整个行业，于是复数也代表一个产业。

senses.title: A short video made for any screen
senses.definition: a short filmed piece made for a phone, a website or a home screen rather than a cinema
senses.definitionCN: 为手机、网站或家庭屏幕而非影院制作的短小影片
senses.example: She made a short movie on her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手机拍了一段短片。
senses.why: Once the word means moving images rather than a cinema release, any screen can host a movie, and length stops being essential.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指的是活动影像而不是影院上映，任何屏幕都能放映 movie，长度也就不再是必要条件。

intro.en: Movie is not an ancient word: it was cut down from moving picture in the early days of cinema and then spread from the screen to the place and the trade.
intro.cn: movie 并不是古词：它由早期的「活动的画面」缩短而来，随后从屏幕扩展到场所与行业。

items.en: The verb movere meant to move or set in motion, and it lies behind the English move inside moving picture.
items.cn: 动词 movere 意为移动、使动，它藏在 moving picture 里的英语 move 背后。

items.en: Old French movoir carried the Latin verb into English use and gave English the plain verb move.
items.cn: 古法语 movoir 把这个拉丁动词带入英语，给英语留下了朴素的动词 move。

items.en: The phrase moving picture was coined when photographs first appeared to move, and it described a new kind of show.
items.cn: 当照片第一次看上去会动时，人们造出 moving picture 这一说法，用来描述一种新的表演。

items.en: American speakers shortened moving picture to movie with the familiar -ie ending also seen in talkie, a film with sound.
items.cn: 美国使用者把 moving picture 缩短为 movie，用了熟悉的 -ie 词尾，带声音的影片 talkie 也用了这个词尾。

items.en: Modern English extends movie from the film itself to the cinema, the outing and the industry, and now to short videos on any screen.
items.cn: 现代英语把 movie 从影片本身扩展到电影院、看电影的出门活动与电影业，如今还指任何屏幕上的短片。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the move stem inside moving picture, while the near-meaning group collects other words for films and their showing.
note.cn: 形近组收「活动的画面」里那条表示移动的词干上的形式，近义组收其他指影片及放映的词。

entries.definition: To change position, the verb hidden inside moving picture.
entries.definitionCN: 改变位置；藏在 moving picture 里的动词。

entries.definition: An act of moving, or an organized group working for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的动作，或为某个目标组织起来的群体。

entries.definition: Changing position, or causing a strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 正在移动的，或引起强烈情感的。

entries.definition: A person who goes to the cinema, often regularly.
entries.definitionCN: 常去电影院看电影的人。

entries.definition: A motion picture, the word more common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 电影，英式用法中更常见的词。

entries.definition: A building where films are shown, or the art of making them.
entries.definitionCN: 放映影片的建筑，或制作影片的艺术。

entries.definition: A film, especially in older or informal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 影片，尤见于较早或非正式的英式用法。

entries.definition: Recorded film material, especially before it is edited.
entries.definitionCN: 拍摄下来的影像素材，尤指尚未剪辑的部分。

normalIntro.en: The word is a clipped compound, and its family keeps returning to the idea of images that move.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被截短的复合词，它的同族词也一直回到「画面会动」这个念头。

normal.en: Movie is moving picture cut short, with the -ie ending that also turned talking picture into talkie.
normal.cn: movie 是 moving picture 缩短而来，用的 -ie 词尾也曾把 talking picture 变成 talkie。

normal.en: The plural the movies names the place and the habit, not a pile of separate films.
normal.cn: 复数的 the movies 指场所与习惯，而不是一堆各自分开的影片。

normal.en: movie theater and movie star are compounds: one names the building, the other the person the screen makes famous.
normal.cn: movie theater 与 movie star 都是复合词：一个指建筑，一个指屏幕捧红的人。

normal.en: A moviegoer is simply movie plus goer, the person who goes.
normal.cn: moviegoer 就是 movie 加 goer，指去看电影的人。

normal.en: Latin movere, to move, sits far back inside the word, which is why the family is full of movement words.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 movere（移动）藏在这个词的很深处，所以这一族词里全是表示「动」的词。

abstract.en: Twenty-four pictures a second make a still photograph stand up and walk.
abstract.cn: 每秒二十四张画面，能让一张静止的照片站起来走路。

abstract.en: A dark hall, one beam of light, and a whole town living inside it for two hours.
abstract.cn: 一间暗厅，一束光，一整个小镇在里面过上两个小时。

abstract.en: The word began as a description of a trick and ended as the name of an industry.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初只是对一种戏法的描述，最后成了一个行业的名字。

examples.en: The movie was shot in a small mountain town.
examples.cn: 这部电影在一个山间小镇拍摄。

examples.en: We go to the movies most Fridays.
examples.cn: 我们大多数周五都去看电影。

examples.en: She wants to work in the movies after college.
examples.cn: 她想大学毕业后进入电影业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木威」——一块木幕上放出很有威势的画面；记住 movie 是电影。

root: 一般认为 movie 是 moving picture（活动的画面）的缩写；moving 源自古法语 movoir、拉丁语 movere（移动），-ie 是英语指小词尾。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the film itself; the senses then divide into the place and the outing, the industry behind it, and the short video on any screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是影片本身；义项由此分出放映的场所与出门活动、背后的产业，以及任何屏幕上的短片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light cutting through a dark hall and landing on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光穿过黑暗的放映厅，落在幕布上。

branches.en: a beam of light crossing a dark hall
branches.cn: 一束光穿过黑暗的放映厅

branches.en: a queue forming outside a cinema
branches.cn: 影院外排起的队伍

branches.en: credits rolling over a crowded studio lot
branches.cn: 片尾字幕滚过拥挤的片场

branches.en: a short clip filmed on a phone
branches.cn: 用手机拍下的一段短片

branches.en: a late show that turns into a night out
branches.cn: 一场深夜电影变成一次夜游

intro.en: The word is a clipped compound resting on a Latin verb of motion, an English ending, and compounds that name the people and the buildings around films.
intro.cn: 这个词是被截短的复合词，依托一个表示运动的拉丁动词、一个英语词尾，以及为人和建筑命名的复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its noun motus name movement, and they are the distant source of the move inside moving picture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 movere 及其名词 motus 表示移动，是 moving picture 里 move 的遥远来源。

definition_zh: 希望；期望；希望的事；（动词）希望；但愿
definition_en: to want something to happen and think it can happen; the good thing that you want to happen
core_image: 黑夜里仍亮着的一根火柴：很小，但朝向光的方向
scene: 考卷发下来之前，她把铅笔盒攥得紧紧的，心里默默念着一定要过。 I hope I pass the exam this time.
sceneCN: 这里 hope 是动词「希望；但愿」（第 1 个义项：盼望好事发生）；发卷前她心里默念希望能通过。

pos.zh: 希望；期望；被寄予希望的人或事

collocations.zh: 往最好处想；抱乐观期待
抱一线希望；明知无望仍存希望

derivatives.zh: hope + -less（无）→ 没有希望的；不擅长的

senses.title: To want something good to happen
senses.definition: to want something to happen and think that it may happen
senses.definitionCN: 盼望某事发生，并认为它有可能发生
senses.example: We hope the rain will stop before the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们希望野餐前雨会停。
senses.why: Hope keeps one eye on the wish and one eye on the chance: it is wishing that feels possible.
senses.whyCN: 希望一眼盯着愿望、一眼盯着可能：是「觉得有可能实现的盼望」。

senses.title: The good thing wished for
senses.definition: the thing or person that people want and look forward to
senses.definitionCN: 人们盼望、期待的人或事物
senses.example: The young players are the hope of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 这些年轻队员是球队的希望。
senses.why: The feeling turns into a thing: what is hoped for becomes the hope itself.
senses.whyCN: 感受变成了实体：所盼望的对象本身就被称为「希望」。

senses.title: To say politely what you want
senses.definition: used to say politely what you want or intend, often to soften words
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地表达愿望或打算，让语气更委婉
senses.example: I hope to see you again soon.
senses.exampleCN: 但愿很快能再见到你。
senses.why: Saying I hope instead of I want makes a request softer and kinder.
senses.whyCN: 用 I hope 代替 I want，请求听起来更温和有礼。

intro.en: Hope is an Old English word, hopian, of Germanic origin; its deeper root is uncertain.
intro.cn: hope 是古英语词 hopian，属日耳曼语源；更深的词根来源不确定。

items.en: Old English hopian meant to wish and to expect good things.
items.cn: 古英语 hopian 意为盼望、期待好事。

items.en: The word belongs to the Germanic family, though relatives outside English are few.
items.cn: 该词属日耳曼语族，但英语之外的同族词很少。

items.en: In Middle English hope worked as both verb and noun, as today.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，hope 与今天一样兼作动词和名词。

items.en: Modern English built the family hopeful, hopeless and hopefully.
items.cn: 现代英语造出 hopeful、hopeless、hopefully 一族。

items.en: The deeper root is not fully agreed on; scholars discuss several old guesses.
items.cn: 更深的词根尚无定论，学界对几种古老猜想仍有讨论。

note.en: Group one holds the hope family; group two holds words about wanting and expecting.
note.cn: 第一组是 hope 词族；第二组是表示愿望与期待的相关词。

entries.definition: feeling that good things may happen
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「满怀希望的」

entries.definition: without hope, or very bad at something
entries.definitionCN: 同根反义词，义为「无望的；不擅长的」

entries.definition: it is to be hoped that; with hope
entries.definitionCN: 同根副词，义为「但愿；满怀希望地」

entries.definition: to want something that may not really be possible
entries.definitionCN: 但愿，所想之事未必可能实现

entries.definition: to think something will certainly happen
entries.definitionCN: 预料，认为多半会发生

entries.definition: to want something strongly
entries.definitionCN: 渴望，语气更强、更正式

normalIntro.en: Use the two opposite endings to fix the word.
normalIntro.cn: 用一对相反的后缀把 hope 记牢。

normal.en: hope + -ful = full of hope, hopeful
normal.cn: hope + -ful＝充满希望＝hopeful。

normal.en: hope + -less = no hope left, hopeless
normal.cn: hope + -less＝希望耗尽＝hopeless。

normal.en: past form hoped keeps only one p: she hoped
normal.cn: 过去式 hoped 只留一个 p：she hoped。

normal.en: hope for the best, prepare for the worst
normal.cn: hope for the best：往最好处盼，做最坏打算。

normal.en: a ray of hope is one thin line of light in the dark
normal.cn: a ray of hope 是黑暗里透出的一线光。

abstract.en: Picture a match struck in a dark room: small, but facing the light.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里划亮的一根火柴：很小，但朝着光的方向。

abstract.en: Picture seeds under snow: nothing shows, yet spring is counted on.
abstract.cn: 想象雪下的种子：什么也看不见，人们却已在数着春天。

abstract.en: Feel hope as a hand half open: not grabbing, not letting go.
abstract.cn: 把希望感受成半开的手：既不抓紧，也不松开。

examples.en: Doctors never give up hope while the patient still fights.
examples.cn: 只要病人还在坚持，医生就不放弃希望。

examples.en: There is still a ray of hope for the lost climbers.
examples.cn: 失踪的登山者仍有一线生机。

examples.en: She hoped quietly that her name would be on the list.
examples.cn: 她默默希望名单上有自己的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厚盼」——心里厚厚地装着一个盼头，就是 hope（希望）。

root: hope 来自古英语 hopian「盼望」，属日耳曼本族词，英语之外同族词稀少，更深词根来源不确定；派生 hopeful、hopeless 等。

sensesIntro.en: Hope moves from the wishing mind, to the wished-for thing, to polite wishes in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: hope 从盼望的心情，到被盼望的对象，再到言语中委婉的意愿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small light still facing the dawn
core.cn: 核心意象：仍朝着黎明的一豆光亮

branches.en: the wish that feels possible
branches.cn: 觉得有可能实现的愿望（义项 01）

branches.en: the person or thing wished for
branches.cn: 被寄予期望的人或事（义项 02）

branches.en: the softening word in speech
branches.cn: 言语中让语气变软的词（义项 03）

branches.en: I hope is kinder than I want
branches.cn: I hope 比 I want 更客气（义项 01 · 03）

branches.en: young players called the hope of a team
branches.cn: 被称为全队希望的年轻队员（义项 02）

intro.en: Hope is a short native verb whose two endings point in opposite directions.
intro.cn: hope 是简短的本族动词，两个后缀指向相反的方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin sperare is the classical verb of hoping; it builds despair and desperate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sperare（盼望）是古典对照动词，派生出 despair 与 desperate。

items.example: I hope the bus is not late.
a hopeful young singer
items.exampleCN: 一位满怀希望的歌坛新秀

items.meaning: without hope; very bad at something
items.example: I am hopeless at drawing.
Hopefully, the rain will stop.

items.meaningCN: hope 的现在分词（去 e 加 ing）
items.example: Hoping for a reply, he checked the mailbox again.
items.exampleCN: 盼着回信，他又查了一次邮箱。

items.meaning: to keep hoping with little reason
items.example: They hoped against hope for news.
items.exampleCN: 他们明知无望仍盼着消息。

items.meaning: to want what may not be possible
items.example: Wish me luck!
Sperare builds despair and desperate.
items.exampleCN: sperare 派生出 despair 与 desperate。

definition_zh: 断层；过错；缺点；故障；责任
definition_en: a break in rock where one side has moved; also a mistake, a defect or responsibility for something wrong
core_image: 一层层岩体被拉开，两侧错位，形成一条可见的裂缝，裂缝两边的高度不再对齐
scene: 多年积累的应力终于释放，岩层沿一条裂缝突然错动。 Movement along a fault released the strain that had built up for years.
sceneCN: 这里 fault 指「断层」（第 1 个义项：岩层两侧发生相对位移的破裂面）；句意为沿断层的运动释放了多年积累的应变。

pos.zh: 断层；过错；缺点；故障；责任
挑出……的毛病；使产生断层

collocations.phrase: through no fault of his own

senses.title: A break in rock
senses.titleCN: 断层：岩层破裂并发生位移
senses.definition: a break in rock along which one side has moved relative to the other
senses.definitionCN: 岩层中的破裂面，其一侧相对另一侧发生了移动
senses.example: Movement along a fault released the strain that had built up for years.
senses.exampleCN: 沿断层的运动释放了多年积累的应变。
senses.why: The geological sense comes from mining: a fault is where a seam of ore fails or is cut off.
senses.whyCN: 地质义来自采矿：断层就是矿层「断掉」或被截断的地方。

senses.title: A mistake or wrongdoing
senses.definition: a mistake or wrongful act
senses.definitionCN: 错误或不当的行为
senses.example: The delay was my fault, not yours.
senses.exampleCN: 延误是我的过错，不是你的。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is 'a failing or defect', which then attaches to the person who caused it.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项是「缺失或缺陷」，后来附到造成缺陷的人身上。

senses.title: A defect in character
senses.titleCN: 缺点：性格或事物上的缺陷
senses.definition: a weakness or flaw in a person's character or in a thing
senses.definitionCN: 人的性格或事物上的弱点、缺陷
senses.example: Generosity is his one fault as a negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 过于大方是他作为谈判者的唯一缺点。
senses.why: A fault is literally a break or gap, so an imperfect character is described as having a break in it.
senses.whyCN: fault 字面就是断裂或缺口，所以有缺陷的性格被描述为身上有一处断口。

senses.title: A technical fault
senses.titleCN: 故障：设备或系统的失灵
senses.definition: a failure in a machine, system or process
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或过程中的失灵
senses.example: A fault in the wiring cut the power.
senses.exampleCN: 线路故障切断了电力。
senses.why: A machine fails where a connection breaks, so the mining sense of a break survives in engineering.
senses.whyCN: 机器在连接断开处失灵，所以采矿中「断裂」的意思在工程里保留下来。

senses.title: Responsibility for something wrong
senses.definition: responsibility for a mistake or for something bad that happened
senses.definitionCN: 对错误或不幸事件应负的责任
senses.example: The driver was at fault in the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在这起事故中负有责任。
senses.why: If a fault is a defect, being at fault means the defect is located in you.
senses.whyCN: 如果 fault 是缺陷，那么 at fault 就意味着缺陷落在你身上。

senses.title: The fault plane
senses.titleCN: 断层面：断层两侧的接触面
senses.definition: the surface along which the two sides of a fault have slipped
senses.definitionCN: 断层两侧沿之滑动的面
senses.example: The fault plane dips steeply to the east.
senses.exampleCN: 断层面向东陡倾。
senses.why: Every fault has a surface of contact, so the noun extends to the geometry of that surface.
senses.whyCN: 每条断层都有一个接触面，因此这个名词也指该面的几何形态。

senses.title: A tennis service fault
senses.definition: in tennis, a serve that misses the legal area
senses.definitionCN: 网球中未落入合法区域的发球
senses.example: She served a fault and had to try again.
senses.exampleCN: 她发球失误，只好重发。
senses.why: The serve fails to land where it should, so the general 'failure' sense survives in sport.
senses.whyCN: 发球没有落到应在的位置，所以「失败」这一通用义在体育中保留下来。

senses.title: To find fault
senses.definition: to criticise small defects in someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对人或事物的小缺陷加以批评
senses.example: He finds fault with every plan we propose.
senses.exampleCN: 他挑我们提出的每一个方案的毛病。
senses.why: Finding fault is literally locating the defect, and the phrase shifted from diagnosis to complaint.
senses.whyCN: find fault 字面就是找出缺陷，这个短语从「诊断」转为「抱怨」。

intro.en: Fault comes from Latin fallere 'to deceive, fail' through Old French. The sense of a rock break grew out of mining language, where a seam 'fails'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fault 经古法语来自拉丁语 fallere「欺骗、失败」。岩石破裂义从采矿用语发展而来，那里矿层会「断掉」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fallere meant 'to deceive, disappoint, fail'; its past participle falsus gave false, and its noun sense of failure underlies fault.
items.cn: fallere 意为「欺骗、令人失望、失败」；其过去分词 falsus 产生 false，而「失败」的名词义构成 fault 的基础。

items.en: Old French faute meant 'a lack, a defect, a mistake'; the form lost the l and gained the sense of blame.
items.cn: 古法语 faute 意为「缺失、缺陷、错误」；这个词形丢了 l，并获得「责备」的意思。

items.en: Middle English restored an l under Latin influence, giving fault, and used it for defects of body, character and action.
items.cn: 中古英语在拉丁语影响下补回了 l，写成 fault，并用它指身体、性格与行为上的缺陷。

items.en: Miners called a break that cut off a seam a fault, and later writers used the word for shortfalls and blame.
items.cn: 矿工把截断矿层的断裂称为 fault，地质学家据此把这个词用于任何发生位移的岩石破裂。

items.en: Engineering added electrical and mechanical faults, sport added the tennis fault, and the phrase at fault fixed the sense of blame.
items.cn: 工程领域增加了电气与机械故障义，体育增加了网球发球失误义，短语 at fault 则固定了「担责」义。

items.en: The step from Latin fallere to Old French faute is generally accepted, but the exact medieval transmission is reconstructed rather than directly documented.
items.cn: 从拉丁语 fallere 到古法语 faute 这一步一般认为成立，但中古时期的具体传播路径是重构的，而非有直接文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to fault; group two holds words for defects and blame that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是形音接近 fault 的词；第二组是表示缺陷与责任但范围不同的词。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'defective'; fault is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「有缺陷的」形容词；fault 是名词。

entries.definition: an arched ceiling or a leap; it begins with /v/, not /f/.
entries.definitionCN: 拱顶，或跳跃；开头是 /v/ 而不是 /f/。

entries.definition: false or imitation, as in faux fur; it is a French borrowing without the final -lt.
entries.definitionCN: 假的、仿制的，如人造毛；它是法语借词，结尾没有 -lt。

entries.definition: failure to do something required, or an automatic setting; the de- prefix adds 'away from'.
entries.definitionCN: 未履行应做之事，或自动默认设置；前缀 de- 增添了「离开」的意思。

entries.definition: an imperfection in a product or a body; it stresses the missing quality rather than blame.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或身体上的不完美；它强调缺失的质量，而不是责备。

entries.definition: a weakness that may be hidden and may ruin something; it is often subtler than a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 可能隐蔽并毁掉某物的弱点；通常比 fault 更细微。

entries.definition: a wrong action or wrong result; it may be accidental and carries less blame than fault.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的行为或结果；可能是无意的，责备意味比 fault 轻。

entries.definition: responsibility for something bad; fault is the defect, blame is the judgement placed on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 对坏事的责任；fault 是缺陷，blame 是加在某人身上的评判。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the word's own history links rock breaks, defects and blame, so the senses can be held together by one image.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个词自身的历史把岩石破裂、缺陷与责备连在一起，因此各义项可用一个形象串起。

normal.en: A fault is a break: rock breaks, a machine breaks, a character has a break, and blame marks where the break is.
normal.cn: fault 就是断口：岩石断开、机器断开、性格有断口，而责备标明断口在哪里。

normal.en: Miners met a fault where a seam stopped, which is how the geological sense was born.
normal.cn: 矿工在矿层中断处遇到 fault，地质义就是这样诞生的。

normal.en: At fault means the defect is located in you, so responsibility follows the image.
normal.cn: at fault 表示缺陷落在你身上，责任便顺着这个形象而来。

normal.en: A tennis fault is a serve that fails to land in the right box, a small failure of the same kind.
normal.cn: 网球 fault 是发球没有落进正确区域，是同一类的小失败。

normal.en: Fault line and fault plane are both built from the geological sense, so learn them as a set.
normal.cn: fault line 与 fault plane 都出自地质义，可以成组记忆。

abstract.en: Abstractly, fault is a discontinuity: something that should be continuous is broken, whether rock, wire or character.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，fault 是一种不连续：本应连续的东西断了，无论是岩石、电线还是性格。

abstract.en: The word moves easily between the physical and the moral because both are read as breaks in a whole.
abstract.cn: 这个词在物理与道德之间移动自如，因为两者都被读作整体上的断口。

abstract.en: Symbol: two blocks offset along a diagonal seam, with a small arrow showing the slip.
abstract.cn: 符号：两块岩体沿一条斜缝错开，旁边一个小箭头表示滑动方向。

examples.en: The San Andreas Fault is a famous example of a transform fault.
examples.cn: 圣安德烈斯断层是一条著名的转换断层。

examples.en: The failure was not entirely his fault.
examples.cn: 这次失败并不完全是他的过错。

examples.en: Engineers traced the fault to a loose connector.
examples.cn: 工程师把故障追查到一处松动的接头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缝特」—— 岩层裂开一条特别的缝，两边错位 → fault 断层、过错

root: 源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失败），经古法语 faute 进入英语，核心含义是「缺失、断口」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fault. The core is a break or gap, which becomes a rock break, a defect, a machine failure or a blame.
sensesIntro.cn: fault 的八个义项。核心是断口或缺口，由此变成岩石破裂、缺陷、机器故障或责备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a break where two sides no longer line up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一处断口，两侧不再对齐。

branches.en: ROCK: a break with displacement, and the surface along which it slips.
branches.cn: 岩石：发生位移的破裂，以及沿之滑动的面。

branches.en: CHARACTER DEFECT: a weakness of character.
branches.cn: 性格缺陷：性格上的弱点。

branches.en: TENNIS FAULT: a serve misses the legal target.
branches.cn: 网球失误：发球未落入合法区域。

branches.en: BLAME: locating the defect in a person, and complaining about small defects.
branches.cn: 责备：把缺陷定位到某人身上，或对小缺陷加以抱怨。

branches.en: SMALL FAILURES: a wrong act and a machine glitch are both a small break in an expected order.
branches.cn: 小失败：做错一件事与机器出一次故障，都是应有秩序中的一个小断口。

intro.en: Fault has a small but productive family: two adjectives, a process noun and the prefixed word default.
intro.cn: fault 有一个小而能产的词族：两个形容词、一个过程名词，以及带前缀的 default。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is fallere 'to deceive, fail' and its participle falsus; Old French faute supplies the noun, and de- plus fallere gives default.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 fallere「欺骗、失败」及其分词 falsus；古法语 faute 提供名词，de- 加 fallere 构成 default。

items.example: The root also gives false and falsify.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也产生 false 与 falsify。

items.meaning: a missing quality or a wrong act
items.meaningCN: 缺失的品质或错误的行为
items.example: The French noun passed into English as fault.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词进入英语成为 fault。

items.meaningCN: 有缺陷的（-y 构成形容词）
items.example: The faulty cable caused the outage.
items.exampleCN: 有故障的电缆造成了停电。

items.meaningCN: 没有缺陷的（-less 表示无）
items.example: Her performance was faultless.

items.meaning: the process of breaking and slipping in rock
items.meaningCN: 岩石破裂并滑动的过程
items.example: Faulting raised the ridge.

items.meaning: failure to act, or the standard setting
items.example: The system returned to its default.
The fault plane dips to the north.

items.meaning: a belt of broken rock around a fault
items.meaningCN: 断层周围破碎岩石构成的带
items.example: The fault zone is several kilometres wide.
items.exampleCN: 这条断层带宽达数公里。

items.meaning: the habit of criticising small defects
items.example: Constant fault-finding wore the team down.
items.exampleCN: 不断的挑剔使团队疲惫。

items.en: Ancient Greek kithara was a professional lyre-like string instrument.
items.cn: 古希腊语 kithara 是一种类似里拉的专业弦乐器。

items.en: Latin cithara borrowed the Greek word for string instruments.

items.en: Old French and Spanish built guitare and guitarra for the flat-backed plucked instrument.
items.cn: 古法语与西班牙语据此造出 guitare / guitarra，指平背拨弦琴。

items.en: French guitare passed the word into English by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪前，法语 guitare 把这个词传给了英语。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling guitar and later added electric guitars.

senses.title: Any person at all

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Any person at all / Someone, in a question.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：任何人、某人（疑问、否定句）。

It gives the sense of a person.

definition_zh: 闪光；闪现；闪光灯；一瞬间
definition_en: a sudden bright light or a quick burst of light; to shine suddenly for a moment; to come or happen very quickly
core_image: 黑暗中骤然亮起又立刻熄灭的一道光
scene: 雷雨夜里，窗外忽然亮起一道白光，紧接着才传来雷声。 A sudden flash of lightning lit up the sky.
sceneCN: 这里 flash 是名词「闪光；闪现」（第 1 个义项：突然亮起又很快消失的光）；句意为骤然一道闪电照亮天空。

derivatives.zh: 由 flash 加 light 构成，义为「手电筒；闪光灯」
由 flash 加 back 构成，义为「闪回；倒叙」
由 flash 加形容词后缀构成，义为「华而不实的；俗艳的」
由 flash 加名词后缀构成，义为「闪光装置；闪烁灯」

senses.title: A sudden burst of light
senses.definition: a sudden bright light that lasts only a moment
senses.definitionCN: 只持续一瞬的强烈亮光
senses.example: A flash of lightning lit the field.
senses.exampleCN: 一道闪电照亮了田野。
senses.why: The core image is light that appears and dies within a blink.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是眨眼之间亮起又熄灭的光。

senses.title: The device that produces light
senses.definition: the lamp on a camera that produces a sudden bright light
senses.definitionCN: 相机上发出骤然强光的装置
senses.example: Turn off the camera flash in the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 在博物馆里请关掉相机闪光灯。
senses.why: The light itself was named first, then the tool that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 先有光的名字，后有制造这种光的器具。

senses.title: A very short moment
senses.definition: a very short period of time
senses.definitionCN: 极短的片刻
senses.example: The answer came in a flash.
senses.exampleCN: 答案一瞬间就来了。
senses.why: Light lasts a blink, so the word measured time as brief as the light.
senses.whyCN: 光只存在一眨眼，这个词于是也用来度量同样短暂的时间。

senses.title: To shine or appear suddenly
senses.definition: to shine suddenly and briefly, or to appear in the mind suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 骤然亮起片刻，或在脑海中突然浮现
senses.example: Her name flashed across the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的名字在屏幕上一闪而过。
senses.why: What flashes in the eye also flashes in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 在眼前闪过的，也在心里闪现。

senses.title: To move very fast
senses.definition: to move past very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 极快地掠过
senses.example: A red car flashed by on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆红车在公路上飞驰而过。
senses.why: Speed so great it blurs looks like light jumping from place to place.
senses.whyCN: 快到模糊的速度，看上去就像光从一个点跳到另一个点。

intro.en: Flash belongs to a family of old English verbs about sudden movement and light.
intro.cn: flash 属于一族关于突然动作与光的老式英语动词。

items.en: Middle English had flashen, meaning to splash or to burst forth suddenly.
items.cn: 中古英语有 flashen，意为飞溅或骤然迸出。

items.en: It is usually tied to a Germanic root for splashing or throwing water, shared with flush.
items.cn: 一般把它联系到一个表示泼溅、抛水的日耳曼词根，与 flush 同族。

items.en: By the sixteenth century flash was used for sudden bursts of light as well as water.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，flash 也用于形容骤然的闪光。

items.en: Nineteenth-century photography gave flash its lamp sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪摄影术赋予 flash 闪光灯的含义。

items.en: Modern media added the flashing news headline and the instant flash of memory.
items.cn: 现代媒体又增添了快讯标题与记忆闪现的用法。

note.en: Flash has close sound neighbours; tell them apart before writing.
note.cn: flash 有多个音近邻居，下笔前要区分。

entries.definition: to turn red, or to rinse with water
entries.definitionCN: 脸红；冲洗；与 flash 音近但词源各有分支

entries.definition: to strike with a whip
entries.definitionCN: 鞭打；睫毛；仅拼写相近

entries.definition: a small bottle for liquids
entries.definitionCN: 烧瓶；细颈瓶；音近词源不同

entries.definition: a sudden memory of the past
entries.definitionCN: 闪回；flash 的复合派生词

entries.definition: to shine on and off quickly
entries.definitionCN: 闪烁；与 flash 的闪烁义相近

entries.definition: to shine with many small bright points
entries.definitionCN: 闪耀；闪烁光芒

entries.definition: a tiny burning piece of light
entries.definitionCN: 火花；火星

entries.definition: a very short time
entries.definitionCN: 片刻；对应 flash 的瞬间义

normalIntro.en: Five quick ways to remember flash.
normalIntro.cn: 五个快速记住 flash 的方法。

normal.en: flash rhymes with splash; both burst out suddenly.
normal.cn: flash 与 splash 押韵，都是骤然迸出。

normal.en: flashlight is a hand torch in America.
normal.cn: flashlight 在美式英语里指手电筒。

normal.en: in a flash means instantly.
normal.cn: in a flash 表示一瞬间。

normal.en: a flash of lightning is the classic nature example.
normal.cn: a flash of lightning 是最典型的自然例子。

normal.en: flashback = flash + back, a scene flashing back to the past.
normal.cn: flashback 由 flash + back 构成，指闪回过去。

abstract.en: See a white line cut the black night sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一道白线划破黑夜。

abstract.en: Hear a camera click and a white blink follow.
abstract.cn: 想象相机咔哒一声后白光一闪。

abstract.en: See a face light up the instant an idea lands.
abstract.cn: 想象念头落下的瞬间面庞一亮。

examples.en: The camera flash woke the sleeping baby.
examples.cn: 相机闪光灯惊醒了熟睡的婴儿。

examples.en: In a flash, the cat caught the mouse.
examples.cn: 转眼间猫就抓住了老鼠。

examples.en: Old memories flashed through her mind.
examples.cn: 往日的记忆在她脑海中闪现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「夫莱什」——夫来一闪就没了：闪光

root: flash 是中古英语 flashen 的延续，一般追溯到日耳曼语中表示泼溅、抛洒的词根，与 flush 同族。水花迸溅与火光迸发画面相通：骤亮骤灭的光（闪光）、制造光的灯（闪光灯）、短如光的时刻（一瞬间）以及快如光的移动。

sensesIntro.en: Flash keeps one idea throughout: something sudden and short, whether light, time, thought, or speed.
sensesIntro.cn: flash 始终围绕同一个概念：骤然而短暂，无论光、时间、念头还是速度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light that bursts and dies in a blink
core.cn: 核心意象：眨眼间迸发又熄灭的光

branches.en: The burst of light itself
branches.cn: 骤然的光本身

branches.en: The lamp that makes it
branches.cn: 制造光的灯

branches.en: Time as short as light
branches.cn: 短如光的时刻

branches.en: Light and thoughts blinking in the mind
branches.cn: 心中闪现的光与念头

branches.en: Speed as fast as light
branches.cn: 快如光的速度

intro.en: Flash builds compounds freely; the list shows its common partners.
intro.cn: flash 能自由构成复合词，下面列出常见搭档。

latinIntro.en: Latin fulgor means lightning brightness; it is a classical parallel, not the source of flash.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fulgor 指闪电的亮光，是古典平行词，不是 flash 的来源。

items.example: He took a flashlight into the cave.

items.meaning: a sudden scene from the past
items.example: The film opens with a flashback.
That is a flashy watch.
The flashing light warned ships.
A newsflash broke in.
A flash flood hit the valley.
Practise words with flash cards.

items.meaningCN: 闪电般的亮光（拉丁平行词）
items.example: Fulgor is Latin for a bright flash.
items.exampleCN: fulgor 在拉丁语中指强烈闪光。

definition_zh: 测试；检验；试验；化验；考查；测验
definition_en: to try something to see whether it works or is true, or an examination and similar trial used to measure quality or knowledge
core_image: 把东西放进火里、放进仪器里，看它到底行不行
scene: 实验台上摆着新电池和一盏小灯。 The engineer used the lamp to test the battery.
sceneCN: 这里 test 是「检验、测试」（第 1 个义项：试验某物以看其性能）；句意：工程师用小灯来测这块电池。

derivatives.zh: 测试员；测试器（test 加表人或表物后缀构成）
测试；检测（动名词，指测试这件事）
易怒的（与 test 无词源关系，仅形近；源自法语 teste「头」）
证明；圣约（源自拉丁 testari「作证」，与 test 同出「见证」意象）

senses.title: Try something to see if it works
senses.definition: to try or examine something in order to discover whether it works or has the wanted quality
senses.definitionCN: 试用或检查某物，以发现其是否有效或具备想要的品质
senses.example: Engineers test every bridge model before building it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在建桥之前会测试每一个桥梁模型。
senses.why: The core image is the trial: something is put under stress so that its hidden quality shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「试炼」：把东西置于压力之下，让隐藏的品质显形。

senses.title: Check a person's knowledge or skill
senses.definition: to give someone questions or tasks in order to measure their knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 给某人出题或任务以衡量其知识或能力
senses.example: The final test covers all five units of the book.
senses.exampleCN: 期末测验涵盖本书全部五个单元。
senses.why: A trial applied to a person becomes an exam: stress is questions instead of weights.
senses.whyCN: 施加于人的「试炼」就成了考试：压力从重物换成了题目。

senses.title: Medically examine a sample
senses.definition: to examine a sample of blood, urine or other material for signs of illness or substances
senses.definitionCN: 检查血液、尿液等样本以发现疾病或物质
senses.example: Nurses will test the blood sample this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 护士今天下午会化验这份血样。
senses.why: Examination under controlled conditions is still a trial, only run in a laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 在受控条件下检查仍是「试炼」，只是搬进了实验室。

senses.title: An examination as an event
senses.definition: a written or spoken examination of knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或能力的笔试或口试
senses.example: She stayed up all night before the driving test.
senses.exampleCN: 驾照考试前她熬了通宵。
senses.why: The act of testing becomes the name of the event in which the act happens.
senses.whyCN: 测试行为转而命名其发生的那场事件。

senses.title: A trial that reveals true quality
senses.definition: a difficult situation that shows what someone or something is really like
senses.definitionCN: 显示出人或物真实品质的困难处境
senses.example: The long delay put everyone's patience to the test.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的延误考验了每个人的耐心。
senses.why: Difficulty works like the laboratory stress: it separates real quality from claimed quality.
senses.whyCN: 困难起到实验室压力的作用：把真实品质与宣称的品质分开。

intro.en: Test comes from Latin testum, an earthen pot used by alchemists to heat metals. Trying metal in the pot became trying anything, and the word drifted through Old French into English.
intro.cn: test 源自拉丁语 testum——炼金术士焙烧金属用的陶罐。在罐中试炼金属演变为试炼一切，这个词经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Testum meant an earthen vessel, especially the cupel in which gold and silver were refined by fire.
items.cn: testum 意为陶器，尤指用火提炼金银的灰皿。

items.en: Assaying metal in the pot gave the metaphor: purity is what survives the fire.
items.cn: 在罐中检验金属形成了隐喻：纯度就是经火之后剩下的东西。

items.en: Old French test kept both the vessel and the trial of metal, and added the sense of proving a claim.
items.cn: 古法语 test 同时保留器皿与试金之义，并加上「证明主张」的义项。

items.en: English took test in the 14th century as a vessel for refining metal, used by alchemists.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 test，指炼金术士提炼金属的容器。

items.en: By the 16th to 17th century the metaphor had won: tests of loyalty, of courage, and finally school tests.
items.cn: 至十六七世纪，隐喻占了上风：忠诚的考验、勇气的考验，最终是学校的考试。

note.en: The first group shows words that only look like test; the second ranks the words English uses for measuring trials.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词；第二组排列英语中各种「测验类」词。

entries.definition: irritable and quick-tempered; the spelling is a coincidence, from a French word for head
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的；拼写巧合，源自法语「头」一词，与 test 无关

entries.definition: proof or evidence; from Latin testari to witness, sharing the idea of proving, not the pot
entries.definitionCN: 证明；圣约；源自拉丁 testari「作证」，共享「证明」意象而非陶罐

entries.definition: to give evidence in court; from the same Latin proving family as testament
entries.definitionCN: 作证；与 testament 同出拉丁「见证」词族

entries.definition: a formal test, often longer and more official; exam is the short form
entries.definitionCN: 正式考试；常更长更正式，exam 为缩略

entries.definition: a short informal test, often for fun or quick checking
entries.definitionCN: 简短随意的测验，常用于娱乐或快查

entries.definition: a test in real conditions, often of endurance rather than knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 现实条件下的试用，常考验耐力而非知识

normalIntro.en: Real links: the alchemist's pot, the gold that survives fire, the blood test, and the driving test.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：炼金术士的陶罐、经火犹存的真金、血液化验、驾照考试。

normal.en: Test began as a pot in which metal was tried by fire.
normal.cn: test 最初是火中试金的容器。

normal.en: Only pure gold survives the fire, so test means finding what is real.
normal.cn: 只有真金经得住火，所以 test 就是找出真货。

normal.en: A blood test is the old pot in modern glass tubes.
normal.cn: 血液化验就是装进现代玻璃管的旧陶罐。

normal.en: Test the water first: dip a toe before diving in.
normal.cn: test the water：下水前先用脚尖试水。

normal.en: Put your patience to the test: the fire now burns your temper.
normal.cn: 「put one's patience to the test」：这一回火烧的是你的脾气。

abstract.en: Every test is a small fire that burns away the claims and leaves the facts.
abstract.cn: 每场测试都是一小簇火，烧掉宣称，留下事实。

abstract.en: Pressure does not create quality; it reveals it.
abstract.cn: 压力不创造品质，它只是显影品质。

abstract.en: A question is a weight placed on the mind to see if it holds.
abstract.cn: 问题就是压在头脑上的重物，看它撑不撑得住。

examples.en: The lab will test the water samples for lead.
examples.cn: 实验室将检测水样中的铅。

examples.en: He passed his driving test on the first attempt.
examples.cn: 他一次就通过了驾照考试。

examples.en: Months of delays tested the team's patience.
examples.cn: 数月的拖延考验着团队的耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴死它」——考试时把答案死死贴在桌上也考不过，还得老老实实测 → test 测试、考验

root: 拉丁语 testum「陶罐、试金灰皿」→ 古法语 test → 英语；由「火中试金」引申出一切测试、考试与考验。

sensesIntro.en: From the alchemist's pot, test grew into trying things, examining people, checking samples, naming the exam itself, and finally any hardship that reveals true quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 从炼金陶罐出发，test 长出试物、考人、验样本、命名考试，最终指一切显露真实品质的艰难处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: metal tried in fire, purity revealed by what survives.
core.cn: 核心意象：火中试金，靠剩下来的东西显出纯度。

branches.en: Trying an object under stress is the oldest branch.
branches.cn: 对物件施压试验是最老的一支。

branches.en: The same trial pointed at a person becomes an exam.
branches.cn: 同一试炼指向人便成了考试。

branches.en: Laboratory checks and exam events carry the pot into modern life.
branches.cn: 化验与考试把陶罐带进现代生活。

branches.en: Hardship is the fire; character is the gold.
branches.cn: 困难是火，品格是真金。

branches.en: What survives the trial is the only honest answer.
branches.cn: 经试炼而存者，才是唯一诚实的答案。

intro.en: Test is short and mostly stands alone; the family adds -er, -ing, and the separate Latin witness family of testify and testament.
intro.cn: test 本身短小、多独立使用；词族加上 -er、-ing，另有源自拉丁「见证」的 testify 与 testament 一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin testum is the pot; a different Latin root, testis meaning witness, gives testify, testament and attestation. The two families share spelling, not origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testum 是陶罐；另一个拉丁词根 testis「见证人」给出 testify、testament 与 attestation。两族拼写相近，来源不同。

items.meaning: a person or device that tests
items.example: A breath tester checks the driver.

items.meaning: the act or process of testing
items.example: Testing of the vaccine took two years.

items.meaning: to give evidence as a witness
items.example: She testified in court for three hours.
His testimony freed the innocent man.
items.exampleCN: 他的证词洗清了无辜者的罪名。

items.meaning: proof; also a will; the Bible's two covenants
items.example: The ruins are a testament to the old city's wealth.
items.exampleCN: 遗迹是古城富庶的证明。

items.meaning: to confirm that something is true
items.example: Experts attested the painting's age.
items.exampleCN: 专家证实了这幅画的年代。

items.example: Students protested the fee rise.

items.meaning: a glass tube for laboratory tests
items.example: The baby was conceived in a test tube.
items.exampleCN: 这个婴儿是试管受孕的。

items.meaning: a case tried to set a legal precedent
items.example: The court chose it as a test case.

latinEntries.meaning: earthen vessel; cupel for refining metal
to bear witness, to make a will

definition_zh: 通常的；平常的；一贯的；惯常的
definition_en: happening or done most of the time, and therefore normal for a person or place
core_image: 每天早上七点同一个座位上一杯同样的咖啡
scene: 清晨的小店刚开门，靠窗那张桌子已经坐上了熟客，点的还是那杯不加水的美式。 He sat at his usual table and ordered the same coffee.
sceneCN: 这里 usual 是「通常的、惯常的」（第 1 个义项：多数时候都如此）；句意为老顾客坐着他常坐的那张桌子，喝着常点的咖啡。每天早上同一杯咖啡的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「通常；一般」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「不寻常的」
同根名词，义为「用法；惯例」

senses.title: What normally happens
senses.definition: describing what happens most often or is most often seen
senses.definitionCN: 形容最常发生或最常见的情况
senses.example: The usual bus is ten minutes late in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨时那班常坐的公交总会晚十分钟。
senses.why: The Latin source names what custom has made habitual, and habit is simply what happens most of the time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁来源指「习俗使之成为常态的东西」，而习惯也就是大多数时候都会发生的事。

senses.title: Customary for one person or place
senses.definition: describing a fixed habit of one particular person, family, or shop
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个人、家庭或店铺固定不变的习惯
senses.example: She took her usual walk along the river after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她照例沿着河走一走。
senses.why: Custom is personal as well as general, so the word also marks the private routines that repeat every day.
senses.whyCN: 习俗既属于众人也属于个人，所以这个词也用来标记每天重复的私人习惯。

senses.title: The ordinary option in a shop
senses.definition: in informal speech, the food or drink one always orders
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指某人每次固定点的那份饮食
senses.example: The waiter brought him the usual without asking.
senses.exampleCN: 服务员问都没问就给他端来了老样子。
senses.why: Once a choice is repeated often enough, it becomes a name in itself, and people simply order the usual.
senses.whyCN: 一个选择重复得够多就成了它自己的名字，人们于是干脆说「老样子」。

senses.title: That is as expected, nothing new
senses.definition: used of an unpleasant event that is exactly what one would expect
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容某件不愉快的事完全在意料之中
senses.example: His usual excuse was that the train was late again.
senses.exampleCN: 他还是那套老借口：火车又晚点了。
senses.why: Because habitual things are predictable, the word easily carries a faint tone of weary expectation.
senses.whyCN: 惯常之事总是可预料的，于是这个词也容易带上一丝厌烦的「又是这样」的意味。

intro.en: From Latin through French: a word about custom and habit, whose base is shared with use.
intro.cn: 经由法语来自拉丁语：一个关于习俗与习惯的词，其词基与 use 同源。

items.en: Usus meant use, practice, and custom; usualis described what custom made ordinary.
items.cn: usus 意为使用、实践与习俗；usualis 形容习俗使之成为常态的事物。

items.en: The form usualis is recorded as an adjective of everyday practice.
items.cn: usualis 这一形式有记录，用作指日常实践的形容词。

items.en: Usuel and the learned usual entered French usage alongside the everyday us.
items.cn: usuel 与书面形式 usual 同日常的 us 一起在法语中并行。

items.en: Usual enters English in the fourteenth century, first in legal and church writing.
items.cn: usual 于十四世纪进入英语，最早见于法律与教会文书。

items.en: The everyday phrases as usual and business as usual make the word home in ordinary speech.
items.cn: as usual 与 business as usual 这些日常说法让这个词彻底扎根于口语。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the use family behind usual, and the near-meaning group gathers words for what is normal.
note.cn: 形近组展示 usual 背后的 use 词族，近义组汇集表示「正常」的一类词。

entries.definition: most of the time
entries.definitionCN: 通常；一般

entries.definition: not common or expected
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常的

entries.definition: to employ something
entries.definitionCN: 使用

entries.definition: the customary way of using
entries.definitionCN: 用法；惯例

entries.definition: as expected or standard
entries.definitionCN: 正常的

entries.definition: plain and unremarkable
entries.definitionCN: 普通的

entries.definition: found or happening often
entries.definitionCN: 常见的

entries.definition: not happening often
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的

normalIntro.en: Think of custom turned into an adjective: what a person or place always does.
normalIntro.cn: 把「习俗」变成形容词来想：某个人或某个地方总是这么做。

normal.en: As usual is a two-word phrase meaning in the normal way.
normal.cn: as usual 是两个词组成的短语，意为「像平常一样」。

normal.en: Business as usual says that nothing has changed.
normal.cn: business as usual 表示一切照旧。

normal.en: The adverb usually is far more frequent in speech than the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 usually 在口语中比形容词本身常用得多。

normal.en: Unusual is the common opposite, formed with un-.
normal.cn: unusual 是用 un- 构成的常见反义词。

normal.en: Usual shares its root with use and usage.
normal.cn: usual 与 use、usage 同根。

abstract.en: Picture the same window seat taken every morning at seven.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早上七点都占着同一个靠窗座位。

abstract.en: Hear a waiter say the usual before you sit down.
abstract.cn: 听服务员在你落座前就说「老样子」。

abstract.en: Notice a worn path across the grass where everyone walks.
abstract.cn: 留意草地上被大家踩出来的一条小径。

examples.en: As usual, she arrived ten minutes before the meeting began.
examples.cn: 像往常一样，她在会议开始前十分钟就到了。

examples.en: He ordered his usual soup and read the paper.
examples.cn: 他点了常喝的那份汤，看着报纸。

examples.en: The shop keeps its usual hours even during the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期里这家店也保持着平常的营业时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优若」——习惯的事做起来总是优若自然，不必多想。

root: 拉丁语 usus（使用、实践、习俗）派生 usualis，经古法语 usuel / usual 进入英语，义为「按习俗常行的」

sensesIntro.en: From custom comes what happens most of the time, then personal routines, then the fixed order, and finally the weary expected excuse.
sensesIntro.cn: 从习俗出发，先指多数时候发生的事，再指个人日常、固定点单，最后是那句听腻了的预料之中的借口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same seat and the same coffee every morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天早上同一张座位、同一杯咖啡。

branches.en: The habit branch: what happens on most days.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：大多数日子都会发生的事。

branches.en: The person branch: this family or shop always does so.
branches.cn: 个体分支：这一家、这一店总是如此。

branches.en: The order branch: the dish repeated until it has a name.
branches.cn: 点单分支：重复到有了名字的那份菜。

branches.en: The excuse branch: expected, and therefore tiring.
branches.cn: 借口分支：全然预料之中，因此令人厌倦。

branches.en: The expectation branch: habit makes events predictable.
branches.cn: 预期分支：习惯让事情变得可以预测。

intro.en: An adjective ending on a stem shared with use, formed in Latin and polished in French.
intro.cn: 一个形容词，接在与 use 同源的词干上，成形于拉丁语，经法语打磨。

latinIntro.en: Latin usus, use and custom, yields the adjective usualis, whose ending -alis becomes English -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 usus（使用与习俗）派生出形容词 usualis，其词尾 -alis 变成英语的 -al。

items.example: The stem us- carries the idea of custom.
items.exampleCN: 词干 us- 承载「习俗」之义。

items.example: Usual means related to custom.
Usually marks what happens in the normal way.
items.exampleCN: usually 标记按常规发生的事。

items.example: Unusual means not customary.
Usualness is rarely needed in speech.
items.exampleCN: usualness 在口语中很少用到。

items.example: Use and usual share one root.
Usage records what custom accepts.
items.exampleCN: usage 记录习俗所认可的说法。

items.example: Custom is the plain English partner.
items.exampleCN: custom 是这个词朴素的英语伙伴。

definition_zh: 行为；举止；待人表现；（事物或动物的）活动方式
definition_en: the way that a person, an animal, or a thing acts in a particular situation
core_image: 一面镜子，照出一个人平时怎么说话、怎么坐下
scene: 课间休息时，教室后排的实习老师在记录孩子们的一举一动。 The teacher watched the children's behaviour in the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 behaviour 是「行为举止」（第 1 个义项：人在具体场合的举动）；句意为老师观察孩子们在操场上的行为。

derivatives.zh: 本词所由来的动词，义为「举止；表现」
由 behaviour 加 -al 构成，义为「行为的；行为方面的」
由 behaviour 加 -ism 构成，义为「行为主义」
由 behaviour 加 -ist 构成，义为「行为主义者」

senses.title: The way a person acts
senses.definition: the way a person acts in a particular situation, as others see it
senses.definitionCN: 某人在特定场合中行动的方式，尤其是别人看到的样子
senses.example: His behaviour at the meeting surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上的举止让所有人吃惊。
senses.why: The noun was built from behave plus -iour, so it turns the act of holding oneself into something others can watch and describe.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 behave 加 -iour 构成，把「把自己拿住」的动作变成别人可以观察和描述的东西。

senses.title: The way one treats others
senses.definition: the way someone acts towards other people, especially in terms of kindness or rudeness
senses.definitionCN: 某人对别人的态度与做法，尤指是否友善或粗鲁
senses.example: Her behaviour towards the new student was kind.
senses.exampleCN: 她对新来的同学很友善。
senses.why: Conduct always points somewhere, and with towards the noun is fixed on the person who receives it, so the sense becomes how one treats others.
senses.whyCN: 举止总是指向某处，加上 towards 后这个名词便固定在接受者身上，义项就成了「怎样对待别人」。

senses.title: Animal behaviour as a pattern
senses.definition: the repeated actions of an animal or group studied as a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 动物或群体反复出现的动作，被当作规律来研究
senses.example: Scientists study the behaviour of birds in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家研究鸟类在冬天的行为。
senses.why: When the same actions repeat under the same conditions, observers stop watching one animal and start describing a pattern, which is the scientific sense.
senses.whyCN: 当同样的动作在同样条件下反复出现，观察者就不再只看一只动物，而是描述一种规律，这就是科学用语里的义项。

senses.title: The way a material or system acts
senses.definition: the way a material, machine, or system reacts under particular conditions
senses.definitionCN: 物质、机器或系统在特定条件下反应的方式
senses.example: The behaviour of the metal changes when it is heated.
senses.exampleCN: 金属受热时，它的表现会发生变化。
senses.why: Once behaviour became a pattern to observe, the same word could describe how a metal or a network responds, so the sense spread from living things to matter.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「行为」成为可观察的规律，同一个词就能描述金属或网络如何反应，于是义项从生物扩展到了物质。

intro.en: Behaviour is an English noun built on the verb behave, with an ending that came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: behaviour 是建立在动词 behave 之上的英语名词，词尾经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Middle English formed the noun from behave plus the ending -iour, which named a way of acting.
items.cn: 中古英语用 behave 加词尾 -iour 造出这个名词，表示「行事的方式」。

items.en: That ending goes back to Latin -atura, a suffix that turns an action into its result.
items.cn: 这个词尾可追溯到拉丁语 -atura，它把动作转成动作的结果。

items.en: Early forms such as havior existed without the be-, and the fuller form later became standard.
items.cn: 早期确有 havior 这类不带 be- 的形式，后来带 be- 的完整形式成为标准。

items.en: American English shortened the ending to -ior, giving behavior, while British English kept behaviour.
items.cn: 美式英语把词尾简化为 -ior，写作 behavior；英式英语保留 behaviour。

items.en: Today the noun covers human conduct, animal behaviour, and the way materials act.
items.cn: 今天这个名词覆盖人的举止、动物的行为，以及物质的表现方式。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family forms and the American spelling; the near-meaning group collects nouns for conduct and manner.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形式与美式拼写；近义组收表示「行为、态度」的名词。

entries.definition: The verb that behaviour was built from.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，是 behaviour 所由来的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行为的、行为方面的」。

entries.definition: The name of a school of psychology built on observed behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行为主义」，一种以可观察行为为基础的心理学派。

entries.definition: A formal noun for the way a person behaves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，正式用语，义为「行为、举止」。

entries.definition: The polite way of acting in social situations.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「礼貌、规矩」，指社交场合中的得体做法。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking or feeling that shows in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「态度」，指表现在行为中的稳定想法或感受。

entries.definition: A single thing that someone does.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动」，指某人所做的单个举动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded formation, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的构词方式、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Behave plus -iour gives behaviour: the act turned into a thing you can watch.
normal.cn: behave 加 -iour 得到 behaviour：把动作变成可以观察的东西。

normal.en: British English keeps behaviour, and American English writes behavior.
normal.cn: 英式英语写 behaviour，美式英语写 behavior。

normal.en: Behavioural is the adjective and behaviourism is the psychology school.
normal.cn: behavioural 是形容词，behaviourism 是心理学流派「行为主义」。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with good, towards, pattern and social.
normal.cn: 它常与 good、towards、pattern、social 搭配。

normal.en: Spell behave plus iour: the verb's letters stay whole, then the ending is added.
normal.cn: 拼写是 behave 加 iour：动词的字母完整保留，再接上词尾。

abstract.en: Imagine a mirror that shows how a person speaks and sits: that is behaviour.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，照出一个人怎么说话、怎么坐下，那就是 behaviour。

abstract.en: Move the mirror from a person to a bird and then to a metal bar: the same picture becomes pattern and reaction.
abstract.cn: 把镜子从人移到鸟，再移到金属条：同一幅画就变成「规律」和「反应」。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the mirror bring the meaning of conduct back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让镜子把「举止」的意思带回来。

examples.en: His behaviour at the meeting surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 他在会上的举止让所有人吃惊。

examples.en: Her behaviour towards the new student was kind.
examples.cn: 她对新来的同学很友善。

examples.en: Scientists study the behaviour of birds in winter.
examples.cn: 科学家研究鸟类在冬天的行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必黑屋」——把人关进黑屋里，才看得清他的行为：行为

root: behaviour 由动词 behave 加词尾 -iour 构成，而 -iour 经法语来自拉丁语 -atura，这个后缀把动作变成动作的结果。因此 behave 的「把自己拿住」变成了可被观察的「举止」。美式英语把词尾简化为 -ior，写作 behavior；今天这个词可用于人、动物和物质。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of behaviour come from one picture: a mirror that shows how something acts when others are watching.
sensesIntro.cn: behaviour 的四个义项都出自同一幅画面：一面镜子，照出某物在别人注视下如何行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror that shows how a person speaks and sits
core.cn: 核心意象：一面照出一个人怎么说话、怎么坐下的镜子

branches.en: THE PERSON: the first sense is simply how one person acts in one situation.
branches.cn: 个人线：第一个义项就是一个人在某个场合怎么行动。

branches.en: THE OTHER: conduct pointed at someone becomes the sense of treating people well or badly.
branches.cn: 他人线：举止指向某个人，就变成「待人好或不好的表现」。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: repeated animal actions become a describable rule.
branches.cn: 规律线：动物反复出现的动作变成可描述的规律。

branches.en: THE MATTER: the same observation moves onto metals and systems as reaction.
branches.cn: 物质线：同一种观察挪到金属和系统上，成为「反应」。

branches.en: THE SCALE: one word covers a single act and a whole studied pattern.
branches.cn: 尺度线：同一个词既指单个举动，也指被整体研究的规律。

intro.en: Behaviour is a derived noun, so the items below are its verb base, its endings, and the parts of its family.
intro.cn: behaviour 是派生名词，下面列出的是它的动词基础、词尾以及词族的各个成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin habitus and mores are recorded words for bearing and conduct; they are parallels to this noun, not its source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habitus 与 mores 是有记录的「姿态、品行」用词，此处作为平行词列出，而非本词来源。

items.example: It forms behaviour from behave.
